Read the file /Users/sinchunyeung/math3033/Textbook/Lebesgue measure-Tao.pdf. I need to find:

1. Section 7.3 (or wherever it discusses "non-measurable sets" / "Vitali set") - what properties does OUTER MEASURE fail to satisfy? The introduction mentions it. Look for content about outer measure not being finitely additive, or any property that outer measure fails but that Lebesgue measure (defined on measurable sets) satisfies.

2. Specifically look for the text in the introduction that says outer measure does NOT satisfy finite additivity.

Return the exact text or a summary of which properties outer measure fails and which properties it does satisfy.
</user_query>

## Outer Measure's Failures (Section 7.3, Tao's *Lebesgue Measure*)

Here's a summary of exactly what you need:

---

### What Outer Measure **Fails** (the key failure)

**It is NOT finitely additive and NOT countably additive.** Specifically:

**Proposition 7.3.1** states:

> "There exists a countable collection $(A_j)_{j \in J}$ of **disjoint** subsets of $\mathbb{R}$, such that $m^*\left(\bigcup_{j \in J} A_j\right) \neq \sum_{j \in J} m^*(A_j)$."

**Proposition 7.3.3** refines this further:

> "There exists a **finite** collection $(A_j)_{j \in J}$ of **disjoint** subsets of $\mathbb{R}$, such that $m^*\left(\bigcup_{j \in J} A_j\right) \neq \sum_{j \in J} m^*(A_j)$."

So outer measure fails **finite additivity** (ix), not just countable additivity (xi).

---

### What Outer Measure **Satisfies** (from Lemma 7.2.5)

From Section 7.2, outer measure $m^*$ satisfies all of (v)–(xiii) **except** the two additivity properties:

| Property | Outer Measure $m^*$ |
|---|---|
| (v) Empty set: $m^*(\emptyset) = 0$ | ✅ Satisfied |
| (vi) Positivity: $0 \leq m^*(E) \leq +\infty$ | ✅ Satisfied |
| (vii) Monotonicity: $A \subseteq B \Rightarrow m^*(A) \leq m^*(B)$ | ✅ Satisfied |
| (viii) Finite sub-additivity | ✅ Satisfied |
| (ix) **Finite additivity** | ❌ **FAILS** |
| (x) Countable sub-additivity | ✅ Satisfied |
| (xi) **Countable additivity** | ❌ **FAILS** |
| (xii) Normalization: $m^*([0,1]^n) = 1$ | ✅ Satisfied |
| (xiii) Translation invariance | ✅ Satisfied |

---

### The Introduction's Key Statement

The introduction (page 73–74) puts it plainly:

> "This approach will almost work, giving us a concept called **outer measure** which can be applied to every set and obeys all of the properties (v)–(xiii) **except for the additivity properties (ix), (xi)**. Later we will have to modify outer measure slightly to recover the additivity property."

---

### Why This Happens (Vitali set construction)

The failure is proven using the **Vitali set** $E$ constructed from cosets of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$. The set $E$ (one representative from each coset of $\mathbb{Q}$) is non-measurable, and the translates $q + E$ for $q \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-1,1]$ are disjoint yet:

$$m^*\!\left(\bigcup_{q \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-1,1]} (q + E)\right) \leq 3 \quad \text{but} \quad \sum_{q \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-1,1]} m^*(q + E) \in \{0, +\infty\}$$

This contradiction shows finite additivity must fail. This construction requires the **axiom of choice** (Section 7.3, Remark 7.3.2).

---

**Bottom line:** Outer measure is sub-additive (always gives an upper bound) but **not additive** for disjoint unions. Lebesgue measure fixes this by restricting to measurable sets only (Section 7.4), where finite and countable additivity are recovered.
